preamble: Diphthongization of the nasal vowel [õ] to the nasal diphthong [ɐ̃w̃] (mapped to the au cell). In Old Galician-Portuguese the word-final outcome of Latin -ōnem and nōn was -om/-on [õ]; during the Middle Portuguese period (15th–16th centuries) it converged with -ão < Latin -ānum, giving modern coração, razão, não. Galician did not take part (corazón, non), so the change is specific to Portuguese.

examples.note: Final -on/-om [õ] converged with -ão; the plural keeps the older vowel in -ões.
Unstressed colloquial /nũ/ preserves a monophthongal variant.

sources: Monte, V. M. do, & Fachin, P. R. M. (2016). Saibham quantos este estormento de contrato virem: análise das terminações nasais em contratos dos séculos XV e XVI. LaborHistórico 2(1): 56–73. https://revistas.ufrj.br/index.php/lh/article/view/4808
Alkire, T., & Rosen, C. (2010). Romance Languages: A Historical Introduction. Cambridge University Press.
